results.title: Jumbo Capex by Telecom Emitters Brings Opportunities and Risks
results.body: Jumbo capex plans by Indonesian telecom issuers are set to reshape the sector, with PT Solusi Sinergi Digital Tbk (WIFI) earmarking Rp7 trillion for 2026 to expand fixed wireless access, fiber‑to‑home, and tower fiberization. PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk (TLKM) has already spent Rp10.8 trillion in the first half of 2026, representing 14.2% of revenue, allocating 94% of capex to core B2C and B2B infrastructure and targeting a 17-19% capex‑to‑revenue ratio. PT Sarana Menara Nusantara Tbk (TOWR) plans Rp2.69 trillion for 2026, split between Rp2.01 trillion capex, Rp47 billion acquisitions, and Rp625 billion ground leases. The article highlights that while TLKM’s mature business model offers defensive growth, WIFI’s aggressive expansion carries higher execution risk and could pressure free cash flow if subscriber targets are not met, with PT Integrasi Jaringan Ekosistem (IJE) noted as a WIFI subsidiary.

results.title: PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk allocates additional 100 MHz spectrum to PT Telkomsel
results.body: PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk announced the allocation of an additional 100 MHz of spectrum to its subsidiary PT Telkomsel, expanding the latter’s 700 MHz and 2,600 MHz bands and raising its total portfolio to 265 MHz. The allocation was disclosed at the Public Expose Live 2026 TelkomGroup on 7 September 2026 to support Telkomsel’s 5G network development. In the first half of 2026 Telkomsel reported revenue of Rp28.0 trillion, up 5.3% YoY, EBITDA up 10.3%, net profit up 24.9%, and mobile ARPU of Rp46 thousand, up 11.6% YoY. The company said the new spectrum will be deployed gradually in line with market demand while maintaining investment discipline and long‑term value creation.

results.title: Telkom Reports 3.9% Revenue Growth in H1 2026, Maintains Full-Year Guidance Amid TLKM 30 Transformation
results.body: Telkom reported consolidated revenue of Rp75.9 trillion for the first half of 2026, a 3.9% year-on-year increase, with normalized net profit rising 6.2% to Rp11.3 trillion. The company's mobile subsidiary Telkomsel posted 5.3% revenue growth to Rp28.0 trillion and a 24.9% jump in net profit, driven by an 11.6% rise in mobile ARPU to Rp46 thousand. Telkom is advancing its TLKM 30 transformation, delayering into five segments and preparing a second-stage spin-off of infrastructure unit InfraNexia in the third quarter, while its data center subsidiary NeutraDC grew revenue 11% to Rp867 billion with 49.9 MW capacity. The group also plans to acquire 100% of Digiserve to bolster its B2B ICT capabilities. Management maintained full-year guidance of 1-3% normalized revenue growth and an EBITDA margin above 50%, noting the second-quarter margin had already exceeded that threshold.

results.title: PT Telkom Indonesia reports H1 2026 net profit of Rp10.6 trillion, up 1.4% year-on-year
results.body: PT Telkom Indonesia (Persero) Tbk reported consolidated net profit of Rp10.6 trillion for the first half of 2026, a 1.4% increase from the same period last year, supported by mobile business strength, operational efficiency, and digital infrastructure growth. Consolidated revenue rose 3.9% to Rp75.9 trillion, while EBITDA grew 3.8% to Rp37.5 trillion with a 49.4% margin. The company's subsidiary Telkomsel contributed revenue of Rp55.6 trillion, up 3.3%, with EBITDA margin expanding 230 basis points to 46.9%. The B2B Infrastructure segment recorded 19% revenue growth to Rp33.1 trillion. Management maintained its 2026 normalized revenue growth target of 1-3% and capex-to-revenue ratio of 17-19%, while targeting completion of the second phase Infranexia transaction by September-October 2026 and evaluating a strategic partnership for its data center business potentially involving a majority stake sale by year-end.

results.title: PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk aims for a 60‑90% dividend payout ratio in FY 2026
results.body: The article announces that PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk plans to allocate a dividend payout ratio of 60‑90% of net profit for its fiscal year 2026, focusing on a year‑end cash dividend with no interim payout. The company’s CFO Arthur Angelo Syailendra said the target range reflects a balance between shareholder returns, expansion needs, and market conditions. Historically, Telkom has maintained payout ratios above 60% since 2013, reaching a record 123.5% in FY 2025 with a dividend of Rp223.17 per share and a total payout of Rp21.19 trillion. For the first half of 2026, the firm reported consolidated revenue of Rp75.9 trillion, up 3.9% YoY, and net profit attributable to the parent of Rp10.62 trillion, up from Rp10.47 trillion a year earlier.

results.title: Foreign investors show early signs of tactical re-entry into Indonesian equities, with analysts highlighting big banks and select sectors.
results.body: Foreign investors are showing early signs of tactical re-entry into Indonesian stocks, with net buying concentrated in large-cap banks during the week of August 31 to September 4, 2026. In that period, foreign net purchases reached Rp1.85–2.3 trillion, led by PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk, PT Bank Central Asia Tbk, PT Bank Mandiri Tbk, and PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk, which together recorded over Rp3.19 trillion of net foreign buying in the regular market. LQ45 outflows have declined sharply from over Rp15 trillion in June to under Rp2 trillion in August, and the number of LQ45 stocks with outflows fell to 27 from 36 in June. Analysts caution this is not yet a structural trend reversal, as year-to-date foreign outflows remain around US$3.94 billion, and sustainability depends on Federal Reserve policy, rupiah stability, and earnings growth. Potential rotation targets include commodity stocks ANTM, AMMN, and INCO, as well as consumer and industrial names TLKM, ASII, INDF, and UNTR, with advisors recommending accumulation on weakness.

results.title: PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk to acquire 100% of PT Digital Aplikasi Solusi (Digiserve) to raise enterprise revenue contribution to 20‑40%
results.body: The article announces that PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk plans to acquire 100% of PT Digital Aplikasi Solusi (Digiserve). The acquisition is intended to strengthen Telkom’s B2B ICT segment and lift the enterprise business’s contribution from less than 15% of total revenue to a target range of 20‑40%. The target was stated by Director of Enterprise & Business Service Veranita Yosephine at a press conference following Public Expose Live 2026 on Monday 7 September 2026. Integration of Digiserve will give Telkom direct control over the solution provider, aiming to deliver end‑to‑end ICT solutions and capture growing market demand.

results.title: PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk opens option to divest majority of data center business
results.body: PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk has opened an option to divest a majority stake in its data center business through a strategic partnership, with the transaction targeted for completion by the end of 2026. The process is currently in the binding‑offers evaluation stage, and Telkom seeks a partner that can provide operational expertise, market access and hyperscaler relationships to accelerate expansion while reducing Telkom’s capex burden. BRI Danareksa Sekuritas estimates the potential sale of about 70% of NeutraDC could be valued between US$1 billion and US$1.5 billion. Proceeds would be allocated to core business investment, balance‑sheet strengthening or additional shareholder returns, and the dividend policy will remain tied to financial performance and shareholder approval.

results.title: Telkomsel’s Rp1 trillion spectrum purchase expected to keep PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk’s 2026 profit intact
results.body: Telkomsel, an entity of PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk, will spend roughly Rp1 trillion to acquire an additional 100 MHz of spectrum (20 MHz at 700 MHz and 80 MHz at 2 600 MHz), raising its total holdings to 265 MHz. CFO Daru Mulyawan said the expense will affect cash flow in the first year but is expected to have limited impact on PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk’s 2026 profit and loss. In Q2 2026 Telkomsel reported revenue of Rp28 trillion, a 5.3% year‑on‑year increase, with mobile ARPU rising 11.6% to Rp46 000 (over Rp47 000 in June) and revenue per MHz growing 5.6% YoY, underscoring the profit‑safety outlook. The subscriber base fell 3.1% to 153.5 million, while the company reaffirmed disciplined capital allocation and continued 5G expansion.

results.title: PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk records Rp322 billion unrealized loss as PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk stock stalls at Rp50
results.body: PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk’s investment in PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk has incurred a large unrealized loss after GoTo shares remained at the Gocap level of Rp50 per share. On Monday 7 September 2026 the shares traded at Rp50 with a volume of 25.20 million shares and a transaction value of Rp1.26 billion, and Telkomsel, as reported in Telkom’s consolidated financial statements as of 30 June 2026, valued the shares at Rp50 each, with the unrealized loss amounting to Rp322 billion. Telkomsel’s CFO Daru Mulyawan stressed that the stock price does not fully reflect the strategic partnership and that the company will continue to evaluate the investment and synergy realization before deciding on further actions.

results.title: PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk targets 60‑90% dividend payout ratio of net profit for 2026
results.body: PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk announced that it plans to distribute cash dividends for 2026 with a dividend payout ratio targeted at 60‑90% of net profit, subject to approval by the shareholders meeting (RUPS). Finance and risk management director Arthur Angelo Syailendra said the payout range will be based on the company’s performance and will be paid after the fiscal year‑end. The dividend policy will be balanced against the firm’s expansion, investment needs, market conditions and shareholder expectations. The final dividend amount will be determined at the upcoming RUPS.

results.title: PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk Discloses 2026 Dividend Policy and Funding Sources
results.body: PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk, the company disclosing the dividend policy, announced its approach for fiscal year 2026, emphasizing attractive shareholder returns while preserving investment capacity and balance‑sheet health. Finance Director Arthur Angelo Syailendra said the policy is underpinned by strong cash flow, disciplined capital expenditure, and potential proceeds from divestments or asset monetization. He added that any funds from divestments or asset sales will be evaluated for use in investments, balance‑sheet strengthening, or additional dividends, with the final dividend amount contingent on financial performance, funding needs, and shareholder approval at the upcoming RUPS. The announcement was made in a virtual press conference on Monday, 7 September 2026.

results.title: Telkom Indonesia acquires 100% of Digiserve to boost enterprise revenue toward 40% target
results.body: PT Telkom Indonesia will acquire 100% of PT Digital Aplikasi Solusi (Digiserve) to integrate it into its B2B ICT segment and strengthen enterprise business synergies. The acquisition aims to increase enterprise revenue contribution from below 15% currently toward the 20-40% range seen at global telecom peers. Digiserve, formerly the Telkomtelstra joint venture, became fully owned by Telkom Group in 2021 and will now shift to direct Telkom control. The transaction remains subject to corporate approvals and satisfaction of conditions precedent. Telkom views the enterprise segment as a key future revenue growth driver.

results.title: Telkom Indonesia (TLKM) Plans to Acquire 100% of Digiserve to Strengthen B2B ICT Segment
results.body: Telkom Indonesia Tbk (TLKM) announced plans to acquire the remaining shares of PT Digital Aplikasi Solusi (Digiserve) to gain 100% ownership and strengthen its Business-to-Business Information and Communication Technology (B2B ICT) segment. The acquisition, disclosed by Digiserve on September 2, 2026, will see Telkom purchase all placed and paid-up capital from current shareholders PT Multimedia Nusantara and Trihono Edhie Laksono. Telkom's Enterprise & Business Service Director Veranita Yosephine stated the enterprise segment currently contributes less than 15% of total revenue, below the 20–40% range seen at global telecom peers, indicating significant growth potential. Digiserve, formerly the Telkomtelstra joint venture with Telstra Corporation Limited, has been fully within the Telkom Group ecosystem since Telkom acquired Telstra's 49% stake in 2021 via PT Multimedia Nusantara. The move aims to create more integrated end-to-end ICT solutions and drive revenue growth in the enterprise segment.

results.title: PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk Announces No Interim Dividend for H1‑2026, Will Pay Cash Dividend After Year‑End
results.body: PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk will not distribute an interim dividend for the first half of 2026 and plans to pay a cash dividend after the fiscal year ends through a shareholders’ meeting. CFO Arthur Angelo Syailendra said the dividend policy balances the company’s performance, expansion and investment needs, market conditions and shareholder aspirations. The company targets a dividend payout ratio of 60‑90% of net profit; for FY2025 it paid a cash dividend of Rp 21.99 trillion (Rp 223.17 per share), a 123.5% payout ratio, with Rp 17.8 trillion from net profit and Rp 4.2 trillion from retained earnings. In FY2024 PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk paid a cash dividend of Rp 21.04 trillion (Rp 212.46 per share).

results.title: PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk announces dividend payout ratio of 60-90% of net profit and allocates over 94% of 2026 capex to core B2C and B2B infrastructure
results.body: PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk announced that its dividend payout ratio for the current fiscal year will be set between 60% and 90% of net profit. The company also disclosed that more than 94% of its 2026 capital expenditures in the first half have been directed to its core B2C and B2B infrastructure businesses. CFO Arthur Angelo Syailendra said the payout range balances dividend growth with the need for expansion, investment, company performance, market conditions, and shareholder expectations. President Director Dian Siswarini highlighted that the disciplined capex allocation helped the company achieve an EBITDA margin above 50% in Q2 2026, supporting stronger profitability and long-term shareholder value.

results.title: PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk commits to 60-90% dividend payout ratio for FY 2026
results.body: PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk announced it will target a dividend payout ratio of 60-90% of its 2026 net profit. The plan was disclosed by CFO Arthur Angelo Syailendra during a public expose on the Indonesia Stock Exchange. For the first half of 2026, the company posted consolidated revenue of Rp75.9 trillion (up 3.9% YoY), EBITDA of Rp37.5 trillion (up 3.8% YoY) with a 49.4% margin, and net profit attributable to the parent of Rp10.6 trillion (up 1.4% YoY). The dividend policy will be balanced against investment and expansion needs and will be subject to approval at the upcoming shareholders’ meeting.

results.title: PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk aims for external customers to contribute up to 30% of PT Telkom Infrastruktur Indonesia’s revenue
results.body: PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk announced that PT Telkom Infrastruktur Indonesia alias InfraNexia is targeting external customers to account for 25‑30% of its revenue, up from the current 10‑15% share. Director Budi Satria Dharma Purba said the commercial push and new partnerships are expected to raise the external contribution to the 30% level. The second phase of Infranexia’s fiber asset transfer, valued at about Rp 35.8 trillion, is scheduled for completion between late September and early October 2026, following the first phase that transferred more than 50% of selected fiber assets from Telkom in December 2025. Telkom Group remains the anchor demand, with Telkomsel serving as a key internal customer for Infranexia.

results.title: PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk plans to acquire PT Digital Aplikasi Solusi, targeting enterprise business contribution of up to 40% of group revenue
results.body: PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk announced it will acquire 100% of the capital of PT Digital Aplikasi Solusi, and Telkom will become the direct controlling shareholder of the IT services provider. The deal aims to raise the share of Telkom’s enterprise business from its current sub‑15% of total group revenue to a target range of 20‑40%, with an ultimate goal of reaching 40% of group revenue. The acquisition, disclosed at a public expose on 7 September 2026 and confirmed by Digiserve on 2 September 2026, is pending corporate approvals under both companies’ articles of association and internal regulations. Existing shareholders PT Multimedia Nusantara and individual Trihono Edhie Laksono will transfer their shares to Telkom as part of the takeover.

results.title: PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk on pace to surpass 2026 targets as first‑half revenue rises 3.9% YoY.
results.body: PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk is on track to beat its 2026 financial targets, with first‑half revenue growing 3.9% year‑on‑year to Rp75.89 trillion, above the company’s guidance range of 1%–3%. The realized EBITDA margin reached 49.4%, close to the minimum 50% margin the company set for year‑end. TLKM attributes the strong performance to its ongoing transformation from an operating‑company to a holding‑company structure, highlighted by the rollout of InfraNexia as an external revenue‑monetisation platform. The first phase of InfraNexia’s monetisation was completed in December 2025, the second phase is underway in 2026, and the final consolidation phase is planned thereafter.
